name: howto
title: Stuck in snow: what the official guidance says
sub: Dig out first; if that fails, stay with the car
footer: Sources: National Weather Service 'During a Storm', CDC tailpipe page (updated August 2026), Minnesota State Patrol column (February 2026). Check your owner's manual before rocking the car.

items.head: Stop spinning
items.body: Spinning digs you deeper and can overheat the transmission.

items.head: Clear the tailpipe
items.body: A blocked exhaust lets carbon monoxide build up inside, says the CDC.

items.head: Dig out the drive wheels
items.body: Clear snow in front of and behind them with the shovel.

items.head: Put traction under the tires
items.body: Sand, mats or even floor mats go in the path of the drive wheels.

items.head: Still stuck? Stay in the car
items.body: NWS: leaving gets you disoriented fast. Call for help.

items.head: Heat in short runs
items.body: NWS: run the motor about 10 minutes an hour, window cracked, exhaust clear.
